name: Does any booking clash
brief:
A lab has one spectrometer, and `slots` lists its bookings as `[start, end]` pairs, each covering the time from `start` up to but not including `end`. Return `True` when two bookings overlap and `False` otherwise. A booking that starts the moment another ends does not clash.

Write `any_clash(slots)`.

Example. In `[[9, 11], [13, 14], [10, 12]]` the bookings `[9, 11]` and `[10, 12]` share the time from 10 to 11, so the answer is `True`.
constraints: $O(n \log n)$ time is the target. Comparing every pair of bookings is too slow.
All tests share a 5-second time limit.
hint: Sort by start. There is a clash exactly when some booking starts before the booking just ahead of it in that order ends.

examples.note: The first and third bookings share 10 to 11.
The second booking starts as the first ends, which is allowed.
One booking cannot clash with itself.

tests.call: any_clash([[2 * j, 2 * j + 2] for j in ((i * 7919) % 200000 for i in range(200000))])

how: Submit runs 12 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value.
notes: Sorting by start brings any clash next to its neighbour: a booking that overlaps a later one also overlaps the one just after it.
Using `<=` in place of `<` is the trap: back-to-back bookings would then count as clashes.
One sort and one pass give $O(n \log n)$ time and $O(n)$ space.
